arxiv-1404-3640.title: Graph-theoretical Bounds on the Entangled Value of Non-local Games
arxiv-1404-3640.creator: André Chailloux, Laura Mančinska, Giannicola Scarpa, Simone Severini
arxiv-1404-3640.description: A 2014 arXiv research paper by André Chailloux, Laura Mančinska, Giannicola Scarpa, Simone Severini. We introduce a novel technique to give bounds to the entangled value of non-local games. The technique is based on a class of graphs used by Cabello, Severini and Winter in 2010. The upper bound uses the famous Lovász theta number and is efficiently computable; the lower one is based on the quantum independence number, which is a quantity used in the study of entanglement-assisted channel capacities and graph homomorphism games.

arxiv-2302-02694.title: Robust Maximum Correntropy Kalman Filter
arxiv-2302-02694.creator: 1 joydeb _ \_ 2121ee32, 2 shovan.bhaumik} @iitp.ac.in 1,2 Indian Institute of Technology Patna (IITP), Patna, Bihar, India
arxiv-2302-02694.description: Abstract The Kalman filter provides an optimal estimation for a linear system with Gaussian noise. However when the noises are non-Gaussian in nature, its performance deteriorates rapidly. For non-Gaussian noises, maximum correntropy Kalman filter (MCKF) is developed which provides an improved result. But when the system model differs from nominal consideration, the performance of the MCKF degrades.

arxiv-2305-13651.title: Adversarial Defenses via Vector Quantization
arxiv-2305-13651.creator: Zhiyi Dong, Yongyi Mao
arxiv-2305-13651.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Zhiyi Dong, Yongyi Mao. Building upon Randomized Discretization [ 38 ] , we develop two novel adversarial defenses against white-box PGD attacks, utilizing vector quantization in higher dimensional spaces. These methods, termed pRD and swRD, not only offer a theoretical guarantee in terms of certified accuracy, they are also shown, via abundant experiments, to perform comparably or even superior to the current art of adversarial defenses.

arxiv-2311-13069.title: FuseNet: Self-Supervised Dual-Path Network for Medical Image Segmentation
arxiv-2311-13069.creator: Amirhossein Kazerouni* 1 Sanaz Karimijafarbigloo* 2 Reza Azad* 3 Yury Velichko 4 Ulas Bagci 4 Dorit Merhof 2,5
arxiv-2311-13069.description: Abstract Semantic segmentation, a crucial task in computer vision, often relies on labor-intensive and costly annotated datasets for training. In response to this challenge, we introduce FuseNet, a dual-stream framework for self-supervised semantic segmentation that eliminates the need for manual annotation.

arxiv-2404-00077.title: A note on the Kronecker–Weyl equidistribution theorem
arxiv-2404-00077.creator: J. Beck, W.W.L. Chen, Y. Yang
arxiv-2404-00077.description: Abstract . We study the relationship between the discrete and the continuous versions of the Kronecker–Weyl equidistribution theorem, as well as their possible extension to manifolds in higher dimensions. We also investigate a way to deduce in some limited way uniformity results in higher dimension from results in lower dimension. 2010 Mathematics Subject Classification 11K38, 37E35 1.

arxiv-2404-08363.title: Let It Flow: Simultaneous Optimization of 3D Flow and Object Clustering
arxiv-2404-08363.creator: Patrik Vacek, David Hurych, Karel Zimmermann, Tomáš Svoboda
arxiv-2404-08363.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Patrik Vacek, David Hurych, Karel Zimmermann, Tomáš Svoboda. We study the problem of self-supervised 3D scene flow estimation from real large-scale raw point cloud sequences. The problem is crucial to various automotive tasks like trajectory prediction, object detection, and scene reconstruction. In the absence of ground truth scene flow labels, contemporary approaches concentrate on deducing and optimizing flow across sequential pairs of point clouds by incorporating structure-based regularization on flow and object rigidity.

arxiv-2410-19076.title: Minimizing Monochromatic Subgraphs of K n , n K_{n,n}
arxiv-2410-19076.creator: Charles Gong
arxiv-2410-19076.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Charles Gong. Given any r r -edge coloring of K n , n K_{n,n} , how large is the maximum (over all r r colors) sized monochromatic subgraph guaranteed to be? We give answers to this problem for r ≤ 8 r\leq 8 , when r r is a perfect square, and when r r is one less than a perfect square all up to a constant additive term that depends on r r .

pmc-11531901.description: Global production of steel and aluminium is a major driver of greenhouse gas emissions. pmc-11621365.title: Myosin VI drives arrestin-independent internalization and signaling of GPCRs
pmc-11621365.creator: Nishaben M. Patel, Léa Ripoll, Chloe J. Peach, Ning Ma, Emily E. Blythe, Nagarajan Vaidehi, Nigel W. Bunnett, Mark von Zastrow, Sivaraj Sivaramakrishnan
pmc-11621365.description: G protein-coupled receptor (GPCR) endocytosis is canonically associated with β-arrestins. Here, we delineate a β-arrestin-independent endocytic pathway driven by the cytoskeletal motor, myosin VI. Myosin VI engages GIPC, an adaptor protein that binds a PDZ sequence motif present at the C-terminus of several GPCRs.

pmc-12752626.title: SIP‐SRS Imaging of Cell Wall Synthesis Identifies a Synergy between Micafungin and Amphotericin B
pmc-12752626.creator: Meng Zhang, Yuewei Zhan, Haonan Lin, Jiyang Chen, Mohamed N. Seleem, Michael Mansour, Ji‐Xin Cheng
pmc-12752626.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Candida species causes life‐threatening infections in immunocompromised individuals and presents a formidable challenge in clinical practice. This challenge is exacerbated by the growing prevalence of drug resistance, particularly against the last resort antifungals such as amphotericin B (AmB). The fungal cell wall, known for its dynamic reorganization in response to growth demands and host threats, are recognized as a key drug target.

pmc-13191556.title: Intermolecular Interactions of Linear Alkane (N ≤ 18) Dimers: A High Accuracy Theoretical Study
pmc-13191556.creator: Chenhui Wang, WanYing Huang, Liang Pu, Zhong Zhang, Robert Bruce King
pmc-13191556.description: This work systematically investigates the intermolecular interactions in n-alkane (C n H2n+2, n = 1–18) dimers through high-accuracy DLPNO–CCSD­(T1)/CBS­(aug2/3)//M05-2X-D3/6-31G** calculations. The relative errors of interaction energies are below 5% with respect to CCSD­(T)/CBS­(aug-cc-2/3)//M05-2X-D3/6-31G** benchmarks. The BSSE-corrected results are reported from −2.2 kJ/mol (n = 1) to −62.6 kJ/mol (n = 18).

pmc-13659661.title: Arterial wall fragment embolism following balloon-assisted coiling: A case report
pmc-13659661.creator: Ryosuke Kaneko, Hiroyuki Ikeda, Mai Tanimura, Minami Uezato, Masanori Kinosada, Yoshitaka Kurosaki, Masaki Chin
pmc-13659661.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Arterial wall fragment embolism is a rare complication of balloon-assisted coiling, and its underlying mechanism remains poorly understood. We report a histopathologically confirmed case of arterial wall fragment embolism during balloon-assisted coiling for a ruptured aneurysm. A 74-year-old woman presented with World Federation of Neurosurgical Societies grade V subarachnoid hemorrhage caused by a ruptured aneurysm at the junction of the right vertebral artery and the posterior inferior cerebellar artery.
